description: Design a 32-bit up counter with an enable input. The counter should increment every clock cycle when the enable input is high and reset to zero when the reset input is high. The counter should also have a synchronous reset. Provide the Verilog code for this counter along with a testbench that tests the functionality of the counter.
code:
module up_counter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire enable,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [31:0] count
);
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 32'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module for a simple Flash memory cell that can store a single bit of data.     input wire RST,    // Reset  
    input wire data_in, // Data to write

);

        data_out <= 0; // Clear the memory cell  
    end else if (WE) begin  
        data_out <= data_in; // Write data to the cell  
    end

endmodule

Design a digital phase shifter that takes a 3-bit input representing a phase (0-7) and outputs a delayed version of that phase using a 4-stage shift register. The output should reflect the delayed phase based on the input value, with each increment corresponding to a delay of one clock cycle.

    input wire [2:0] phase_in,
    output reg [2:0] phase_out
);
    reg [2:0] shift_reg [0:3]; // 4-stage shift register

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // Shift the input phase through the register
        shift_reg[0] <= phase_in;           // Input phase
        shift_reg[1] <= shift_reg[0];       // First stage delay
        shift_reg[2] <= shift_reg[1];       // Second stage delay
        shift_reg[3] <= shift_reg[2];       // Third stage delay

    end
endmodule

A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) that generates a frequency based on a control input value. The output frequency should double for every increment of the input control signal. The design will use a simple counter to represent the frequency output based on the control signal. The control input will vary between 0 and 4, representing different frequency states.

module vco (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [2:0] control, // 3-bit control input
    output reg [3:0] freq_out // 4-bit frequency output
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            freq_out <= 4'b0000; // Reset frequency output
        end else begin
            case (control)
                3'b000: freq_out <= 4'b0001; // 1
                3'b001: freq_out <= 4'b0010; // 2
                3'b010: freq_out <= 4'b0100; // 4
                3'b011: freq_out <= 4'b1000; // 8

endmodule

description: Design a D-latch in Verilog that captures the value of the data input (D) when the enable signal (E) is high. When E is low, the output (Q) should hold its last value. Additionally, create a complementary output (Q_bar) which is the inverse of Q.

    input wire clock,
    output reg serial_output
);

    input [3:0] a11, a12,
    input [3:0] a21, a22,
    output [3:0] l11, l12, l21, l22,
    output [3:0] u11, u12, u21, u22
);

// Intermediate signals for calculations
wire [3:0] l21_temp; // Temporary variable for L(2,1)
wire [3:0] u11_temp; // Temporary variable for U(1,1)

// Calculate L and U matrices
assign l11 = 4'b0001; // L(1,1) is always 1
assign l12 = 4'b0000; // L(1,2) is 0
assign l21_temp = a21 / a11; // L(2,1) = A(2,1) / A(1,1)
assign l21 = l21_temp; // L(2,1)
assign l22 = 4'b0001; // L(2,2) is always 1

assign u11 = a11; // U(1,1) = A(1,1)
assign u12 = a12; // U(1,2) = A(1,2)
assign u21 = 4'b0000; // U(2,1) is 0
assign u22 = a22 - (l21_temp * u12); // U(2,2) = A(2,2) - L(2,1) * U(1,2)

endmodule

The output voltage should be controlled based on the comparison with a reference voltage. Implement a simple state machine to manage the control of the switch.
code:
module LDO_Controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] Vin,        // Input voltage
    input wire [7:0] Vref,       // Reference voltage
    output reg switch_ctrl,       // Control signal for the switch
    output reg [7:0] Vout         // Output voltage
);

                    ON = 2'b01, 
                    OFF = 2'b10; 
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) 
            state <= IDLE;
        else 
            state <= next_state;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)

description: Design a simple Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) using a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR). The generator should take a 4-bit seed as input and produce a 4-bit random output. The feedback polynomial to be used is x^4 + x^3 + 1.
code:
module csprng (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] seed,
    output reg [3:0] random_out
);
    reg [3:0] lfsr;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            lfsr <= seed; // load the initial seed
            random_out <= seed; // initial output is the seed
        end else begin
            lfsr <= {lfsr[2:0], lfsr[3] ^ lfsr[2]}; // feedback

endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that takes three 5-bit inputs representing three different investment opportunities and produces a 5-bit output that represents the optimal investment strategy. The optimal strategy is determined by taking the bitwise AND of the three input values. This will signify which investments should be made (1) and which should not (0).

Design a Pulse Width Modulator (PWM) that generates a PWM signal based on a given duty cycle and clock input. The PWM signal should toggle based on the clock and the duty cycle input. The duty cycle input will be a value between 0 and 255, where 0 means 0% duty cycle and 255 means 100% duty cycle.
code:
module pwm_generator (

    input wire rst,          // Reset input
    input wire [7:0] duty,   // 8-bit duty cycle input

);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin

            pwm <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (counter < duty) begin
                pwm <= 1'b1;
            end else begin
                pwm <= 1'b0;

description: Design a 4-bit Carry-Save Adder (CSA) that takes three 4-bit inputs (A, B, C) and computes the sum and carry outputs. The sum output should be a 4-bit result and the carry output should be a 4-bit result as well. Ensure that your design is efficient and can be simulated easily.

Design an echo cancellation system that processes a continuous input signal and removes an echo effect based on a previous sample. description:
Design a JK latch using Verilog. The JK latch should have two inputs J and K, one clock input CLK, and one output Q. The latch should operate as follows: 
- If J = K = 0, Q remains unchanged.
- If J = 1 and K = 0, Q is set to 1.
- If J = 0 and K = 1, Q is reset to 0.
- If J = K = 1, Q toggles its state.
code:
module jk_latch (
    input J,
    input K,
    input CLK,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        if (J == 0 && K == 0) Q <= Q; // Maintain previous state
        else if (J == 1 && K == 0) Q <= 1; // Set Q
        else if (J == 0 && K == 1) Q <= 0; // Reset Q
        else if (J == 1 && K == 1) Q <= ~Q; // Toggle Q
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit DRAM cell with the following functionality: The cell has a 16-bit data input (din), a 16-bit data output (dout), a read enable signal (read_en), a write enable signal (write_en), and a clock signal (clk). Design a 4-bit divider that takes a 4-bit dividend and a 4-bit divisor as inputs and produces a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder as outputs. Design an 8-bit DRAM cell that can be read from and written to. The DRAM cell should have the following inputs and outputs:

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple gradient descent algorithm to find the minimum of a quadratic function f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c. Design an 8-bit divider that takes two 8-bit binary numbers as inputs (dividend and divisor) and produces an 8-bit quotient and an 8-bit remainder as outputs. The division should be performed using combinational logic.

Design a Watchdog Timer that resets the system if a specific signal (e.g., 'reset_signal') is not asserted within a certain timeout period. The timer should have an input clock, a reset signal, and an output that indicates whether the system is in a safe state (active) or has been reset (inactive). The timer should be implemented using a counter that counts clock cycles until the reset signal is asserted, and then resets the system if the limit is exceeded.
code:
module WatchdogTimer(  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire reset_signal,  
    output reg system_reset  
);  
    parameter TIMEOUT_LIMIT = 100; // Define the timeout limit  
    reg [6:0] counter; // 7-bit counter to keep track of clock cycles  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset_signal) begin  
        if (reset_signal) begin  
            counter <= 0;  
            system_reset <= 0; // System is safe  
        end else if (counter < TIMEOUT_LIMIT) begin  
            counter <= counter + 1;  
            system_reset <= 0; // System is safe  
        end else begin  
            system_reset <= 1; // System reset triggered  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

Design a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog that takes an input clock signal and generates an output clock signal that is a frequency-multiplied version of the input clock.     parameter MEASUREMENT_DIM = 2
)(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [15:0] z1, // measurement from sensor 1
    input [15:0] z2, // measurement from sensor 2
    input [15:0] A, // state transition matrix (flattened)
    input [15:0] H, // measurement matrix (flattened)
    input [15:0] Q, // process noise covariance (flattened)
    input [15:0] R, // measurement noise covariance (flattened)
    output reg [15:0] x_est, // estimated state
    output reg [15:0] p_est // estimated covariance
);

    reg [15:0] p_pred;
    reg [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

        if (reset) begin
            x_est <= 0;
            p_est <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            x_pred <= A * x_est; // State prediction
            p_pred <= A * p_est * A + Q; // Covariance prediction
            
            // Update step
            K <= p_pred * H / (H * p_pred * H + R); // Kalman gain
            x_est <= x_pred + K * (z1 + z2 - H * x_pred); // Update state estimate
            p_est <= (1 - K * H) * p_pred; // Update covariance estimate
        end
    end
endmodule

description:

- Inputs: `data_in` (1-bit), `write_enable` (1-bit), `read_enable` (1-bit)
- Outputs: `data_out` (1-bit)

The behavior is as follows:
- When `write_enable` is high, the value of `data_in` should be stored.
- When `read_enable` is high, the stored value should be output to `data_out`.
- If neither `write_enable` nor `read_enable` is high, the stored value remains unchanged.

Design a 16-bit DRAM cell type that has an input for data (16 bits) and a control signal (write_enable). When write_enable is high, the input data is stored in the memory cell. There should also be an output that reflects the stored data.

Design a combinational logic module in Verilog that computes the parameters of a simple linear regression model given a set of input data points. The module should take as inputs the x and y values of the data points, and output the slope (m) and y-intercept (b) of the regression line. Assume the module processes 5 data points at a time.

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple NAT function. The module takes a 32-bit source IP address and a corresponding port number as inputs and outputs a translated IP address and port number. The translation is predefined: the source IP 192.168.1.1 is translated to 10.0.0.1, and port 8080 is translated to port 9090.

Design a 4-bit shift register with the following specifications: The shift register should support both left and right shifts, with the ability to load a new 4-bit value on a load signal. The shift direction is controlled by a control signal: when the control signal is high, the register should shift left; when low, it should shift right. If the load signal is active, the register should load the input value instead of shifting.
code:
module shift_register (  
    input clk,  
    input load,  
    input dir,  
    input [3:0] data_in,  
    output reg [3:0] data_out  
);  
    always @(posedge clk) begin  
        if (load) begin  
            data_out <= data_in;  
        end else if (dir) begin  
            data_out <= {data_out[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left  
        end else begin  
            data_out <= {1'b0, data_out[3:1]}; // Shift right  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a simple Flash memory cell model using Verilog. The memory cell should have the following inputs: `write_enable`, `data_in`, and `read_enable`, and one output `data_out`. The cell should store a single bit of data. When `write_enable` is high, the `data_in` should be stored. When `read_enable` is high, the stored data should be output to `data_out`.

Design a simple audio frame decoder that reads a 32-bit audio frame input and extracts the 16-bit sample rate and 16-bit channel count from it. The input format is as follows: the 32-bit input is structured as [15:0] = sample rate, [31:16] = channel count. The output should be two separate 16-bit values for the sample rate and channel count.

Design a 2-bit divider in Verilog that takes a 2-bit numerator and a 2-bit denominator as inputs and outputs a 2-bit quotient and a 2-bit remainder. The design should handle division by zero by setting the quotient and remainder to 0 in that case.

Design a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue in Verilog. The FIFO should have a parameterized depth, with the following functionalities:
- Enqueue: Add data to the queue.
- Dequeue: Remove data from the queue.
- Check if the queue is empty.
- Check if the queue is full.
Implement appropriate control signals for enqueue and dequeue operations, along with a reset signal.

Design a 16-bit DRAM cell with the following functionality: it should have a 16-bit input data bus (data_in), a 16-bit output data bus (data_out), a write enable signal (we), and a clock signal (clk). When we is high, data_in should be written to the DRAM cell on the rising edge of clk. When we is low, data_out should reflect the stored data in the DRAM cell on the falling edge of clk.

Design a fan speed control system that adjusts the speed of the fan based on the temperature input. The system should have two inputs: a 4-bit temperature reading and a 2-bit control signal. The fan speed output should be a 3-bit value that represents the fan speed. Based on the temperature, the fan speed should be determined as follows: if temperature < 50, speed = 3'b000 (off); if 50 <= temperature < 70, speed = 3'b001 (low); if 70 <= temperature < 90, speed = 3'b010 (medium); if temperature >= 90, speed = 3'b011 (high). The control signal can be used to enable or disable the fan. If control signal is '00', the fan is off regardless of temperature. If control signal is '01', the fan operates according to the temperature. If control signal is '10' or '11', the fan operates continuously at medium speed regardless of temperature.
code:
module fan_speed_control (
    input [3:0] temperature,
    input [1:0] control,
    output reg [2:0] fan_speed
);

    always @(temperature or control) begin
        case (control)
            2'b00: fan_speed = 3'b000; // Fan off
            2'b01: begin // Control by temperature
                if (temperature < 4'd50)
                    fan_speed = 3'b000; // Off
                else if (temperature < 4'd70)
                    fan_speed = 3'b001; // Low
                else if (temperature < 4'd90)
                    fan_speed = 3'b010; // Medium
                else
                    fan_speed = 3'b011; // High
            end
            2'b10: fan_speed = 3'b010; // Medium speed
            2'b11: fan_speed = 3'b010; // Medium speed
            default: fan_speed = 3'b000; // Default to off
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a pulse generator that generates a pulse of width N clock cycles. The pulse should start on the rising edge of the input signal 'start' and should be output on 'pulse'. The pulse should remain high for N clock cycles and then return low.

Implement a simple Kalman filter in Verilog. The Kalman filter should estimate the state of a system given noisy measurements. The filter will have inputs for the measurement, process noise covariance, measurement noise covariance, and the previous state estimate. The output will be the updated state estimate.

Design a 4-bit SRAM cell that includes a write enable (WE), a read enable (RE), and an output enable (OE). The cell should be able to store a 4-bit value and allow reading and writing based on the control signals. Implement the necessary logic to ensure correct behavior during read and write operations.
code:
module sram_cell (
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    input wire WE, 
    input wire RE,
    input wire OE,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] storage;

    always @(posedge WE or posedge RE) begin
        if (WE) begin
            storage <= data_in; // Write data to storage
        end
        if (RE) begin
            data_out <= storage; // Read data from storage
        end
    end

    always @(OE) begin
        if (OE) begin
            data_out <= storage; // Output data when OE is high
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit parallel input and outputs a serialized 1-bit stream. The serializer should operate on a clock signal and have a load signal to indicate when to load new data. The output should shift out the bits one at a time on each clock cycle.
code:
module serializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [7:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);

    reg [2:0] bit_index; // 3 bits to count from 0 to 7

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            bit_index <= 3'b111; // Start from the highest bit
        end else if (bit_index != 3'b111) begin
            serial_out <= parallel_in[bit_index]; // Shift out the current bit
            bit_index <= bit_index - 1; // Move to the next bit
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Carry-Skip Adder (CSA) in Verilog. The CSA should take two n-bit binary numbers and a carry-in bit as inputs and produce an n-bit sum and a carry-out bit. The implementation should allow for configurable bit-width during instantiation.

Create a 32-bit ALU that can perform the following operations based on a 3-bit control signal:
- 000: ADD
- 001: SUB
- 010: AND
- 011: OR
- 100: XOR
- 101: NAND
- 110: NOR
- 111: XNOR
The ALU should take two 32-bit inputs and provide a 32-bit output along with a zero flag that indicates if the output is zero.
code:
module ALU (
    input [31:0] A,
    input [31:0] B,
    input [2:0] ALUOp,
    output reg [31:0] Result,
    output reg Zero
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (ALUOp)
            3'b000: Result = A + B;        // ADD
            3'b001: Result = A - B;        // SUB
            3'b010: Result = A & B;        // AND
            3'b011: Result = A | B;        // OR
            3'b100: Result = A ^ B;        // XOR
            3'b101: Result = ~(A & B);     // NAND
            3'b110: Result = ~(A | B);     // NOR
            3'b111: Result = ~(A ^ B);     // XNOR
            default: Result = 32'h00000000; // Default case
        endcase
        Zero = (Result == 32'h00000000) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0; // Set Zero flag
    end
endmodule

description: Create a simple Ethernet MAC controller state machine that transitions between IDLE, RECEIVE, and TRANSMIT states. The state machine should trigger state transitions based on input signals: `start_receive` and `start_transmit`. Implement the state transitions using a clock signal.

Create a 32-bit up-counter with enable and reset functionality. The counter should count upwards on every clock cycle when the enable signal is high. If the reset signal is high, the counter should reset to zero regardless of the enable signal. The counter should be able to wrap around from 32'hFFFFFFFF to 32'h00000000.
code:
module counter_32bit (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    output reg [31:0] count
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 32'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the A* search algorithm. The module should take as input the current node, the goal node, the cost to reach the current node, and the heuristic estimate to the goal node. The output should be the next node to explore based on the shortest path determined by the A* algorithm. You may assume a small fixed number of nodes (e.g., 4 nodes) for simplicity.

Design a Watchdog Timer in Verilog. The Watchdog Timer should have a reset input, a clock input, and a timeout output. The timer should start counting when the reset signal is low and should output a timeout signal if it does not receive a reset signal within a specified number of clock cycles. The timeout condition can be set by a parameter that defines the number of clock cycles before the timeout occurs.

Design a Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller in Verilog. The DMA controller will have the following inputs and outputs:
- Inputs:
  - start: A signal to start the DMA transfer (1-bit)
  - addr: A 16-bit address for the data transfer
  - data_in: A 16-bit input data line
  - clk: A clock signal
  - reset: A reset signal (active high)
- Outputs:
  - data_out: A 16-bit output data line
  - done: A signal indicating the transfer is complete (1-bit)

The DMA controller should perform the following functions:
- When reset is asserted, the controller should initialize its state.
- When the start signal is asserted, the controller should transfer data from data_in to the memory address specified by addr and assert done when the transfer is complete.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input wire start,
    input wire [15:0] addr,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [15:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);

reg [1:0] state;
localparam IDLE = 2'b00,
           TRANSFER = 2'b01,
           DONE = 2'b10;

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        state <= IDLE;
        data_out <= 16'b0;
        done <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                if (start) begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Transfer data
                    state <= TRANSFER;
                    done <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
            TRANSFER: begin
                // Simulate data transfer to the address (not implemented in hardware)
                state <= DONE;
            end
            DONE: begin
                done <= 1'b1; // Indicate transfer is done
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
            end
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

description: Create a 32-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit input word and serializes it into a 32-bit output. The serialization should occur on a clock edge, with the output shifting left by one bit for each incoming input word. The serializer should output the last 8 bits received after 4 clock cycles.

Design a simple watchdog timer that resets after a specified timeout period. The timer should start counting when an enable signal is asserted. If the timer reaches the timeout value without being reset, it should output a reset signal.

Design a 2-to-4 decoder. The decoder has 2 input lines (A1, A0) and 4 output lines (Y0, Y1, Y2, Y3). The output lines should represent the binary value of the input lines. For example, if A1A0 = 00, then Y0 = 1 and Y1, Y2, Y3 = 0; if A1A0 = 01, then Y1 = 1 and Y0, Y2, Y3 = 0, and so on.

Create a reset controller that can handle two types of reset signals: an active low reset and a synchronous reset. The output should hold its value on the rising edge of the clock unless the reset signal is activated. When the reset is activated, the output should be reset to 0.
code:
module reset_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n, // Active low reset
    input wire sync_rst, // Synchronous reset
    output reg out
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            out <= 0; // Asynchronous reset
        end else if (sync_rst) begin
            out <= 0; // Synchronous reset
        end
    end

endmodule

description:
Design a simple GPIO controller that can read input signals and set output signals based on a clock signal. The GPIO controller should have the following functionality:
1. It should have a 5-bit input for reading GPIO states.
2. It should have a 5-bit output for setting GPIO states.
3. The output should be set to the input value on the rising edge of the clock.
4. There should be an enable signal that allows the output to change only when it is high.
code:
module gpio_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [4:0] gpio_in,
    output reg [4:0] gpio_out
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (enable) begin
            gpio_out <= gpio_in;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple LZW compression encoder in Verilog that takes a stream of 8-bit input data and compresses it into a stream of variable-length encoded output. The encoder should maintain a dictionary of previously encountered sequences and generate the corresponding code for each sequence in the input. The output should be a sequence of encoded values.

Design a 32-tap FIR filter that takes a 16-bit signed input sample and produces a 16-bit signed output sample. The filter coefficients are predefined and should be implemented as a memory array. The design should shift the input samples into the filter and compute the output as the sum of the products of the input samples with the corresponding coefficients.

Design a module that implements a simple DES-like encryption algorithm. The module should accept a 64-bit plaintext input and a 64-bit key input, then produce a 64-bit ciphertext output after a specified number of rounds (for simplicity, use 3 rounds in this example). The encryption should be based on a simplified Feistel network structure.

Design a reset controller that detects a reset signal and produces a reset output. The reset output should remain active for a specified number of clock cycles after the reset signal is asserted, and then it should deactivate.

Design a 2-channel DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller that can transfer data from a source address to a destination address. The controller should have the following features:
- Two channels, each with a source address, destination address, and a transfer size.
- A start signal to initiate the transfer for the selected channel.
- An output signal indicating the completion of the transfer.
- A reset signal to initialize the controller.

Design a virtual memory address translation module that takes a logical address and translates it to a physical address using a simple page table. Assume a page size of 4KB and that the page table entry is 32 bits. The logical address will be 32 bits, and the module should be able to handle 256 pages in the page table. The module should have a clock input for synchronization and a reset input to clear the state. Implement the address translation logic and output the physical address.
code:
module virtual_memory_translation (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [31:0] logical_address,
    input [255:0] page_table, // 256 entries, each 32 bits wide
    output reg [31:0] physical_address,
    output reg valid
);
    reg [7:0] page_number; // 8 bits for page number (0-255)
    reg [11:0] offset;     // 12 bits for offset (0-4095)

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            physical_address <= 32'b0;
            valid <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            page_number <= logical_address[31:24]; // Get the page number from logical address
            offset <= logical_address[11:0];       // Get the offset from logical address
            
            // Check if the page number is valid
            if (page_number < 256) begin
                physical_address <= {page_table[page_number*32 +: 20], offset}; // Concatenate page frame number with offset
                valid <= 1'b1;
            end else begin
                valid <= 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit SRAM cell that can store a value and read it back. The SRAM cell should have a write enable signal to control when to write data, and a read enable signal to control when to read data. The SRAM cell should have inputs for the data to be written, an address to select the cell, and outputs for the data read from the cell.
code:
module sram_8bit (
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire [2:0] address,
    input wire we,  // write enable
    input wire re,  // read enable
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    reg [7:0] memory [0:7]; // 8-bit wide and 8 locations

    always @(posedge we) begin
        memory[address] <= data_in; // write data
    end

    always @(posedge re) begin
        data_out <= memory[address]; // read data
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit adder in Verilog that takes two 32-bit unsigned integers as inputs and produces a 32-bit sum as output. The adder should also have a carry-out output to indicate if there is an overflow.

Design a 3-input AND gate using Verilog. The AND gate should output high (1) only when all three inputs are high (1). Implement the module and provide a testbench to verify its functionality using predefined test cases from a file.

Create a 256-bit AES encryption module that takes a 256-bit plaintext and a 256-bit key as inputs and produces a 256-bit ciphertext as output. The module should implement a simplified version of the AES encryption algorithm, focusing on the key addition step and four rounds of substitution and permutation. Ensure it includes necessary registers to hold the state and the round key.

Design an 8-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit parallel input and serializes it into a single output bit stream. The serialization occurs on a clock edge, and a valid signal indicates when the output is valid. The serializer should also have a reset feature to initialize the state.
code:
module serializer(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] parallel_in,
    input wire valid,
    output reg serial_out
);

    reg [2:0] bit_index; // 3 bits to count from 0 to 7

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_index <= 3'b000;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
        end else if (valid) begin
            if (bit_index < 3'b111) begin
                serial_out <= parallel_in[7 - bit_index]; // Sending bits from MSB to LSB
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
            end else begin
                serial_out <= 1'b0; // Default output when all bits are sent
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple JPEG compression block that takes a 4x4 pixel block (representing grayscale values) as input and outputs a simplified version of the DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) coefficients as outputs. The input is a 16-bit vector where each 4 bits represent one pixel value. The output should be a 32-bit vector representing the DCT coefficients of the 4x4 block.
code:
module jpeg_dct (

);
    // DCT calculation simplified for educational purposes

        dct_coeffs[47:32] = pixel_block[47:32]; // Placeholder
        dct_coeffs[63:48] = pixel_block[63:48]; // Placeholder
        dct_coeffs[79:64] = 16'b0; // Placeholder for more coefficients
        dct_coeffs[95:80] = 16'b0; // Placeholder
        dct_coeffs[111:96] = 16'b0; // Placeholder
        dct_coeffs[127:112] = 16'b0; // Placeholder
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller that can receive and transmit frames. The MAC controller should have the following inputs: `clk`, `reset`, `rx_data`, `rx_valid`, and `tx_data`, with outputs `tx_valid` and `tx_ready`. The design should implement a simple state machine to handle the reception and transmission of data.

Design a temperature monitoring system that uses a flip-flop to store the current temperature. The system should take a 5-bit binary input representing the temperature in degrees Celsius. If the temperature exceeds a threshold of 25 degrees (represented as 11001 in binary), an alert signal (1-bit output) should be set high. The system should have a clock and a reset signal. On the rising edge of the clock, if reset is low, it updates the stored temperature and evaluates the alert; if reset is high, it should clear the stored temperature and the alert.

Design a 4-channel DMA controller that can handle data transfers from multiple sources to a single destination. The DMA controller should have the following inputs: 
- `req`: a 4-bit request signal indicating which channel is requesting access (0-3).
- `ack`: a 4-bit acknowledgement signal for the channels.
- `clk`: clock signal.
- `reset`: active high reset signal.

The DMA controller should provide an output `active_channel`, which indicates which channel is currently active for data transfer. The controller should sequentially grant access to the channels based on the request signals, prioritizing lower-numbered channels in case of simultaneous requests. On reset, `active_channel` should be set to 4'b0000.
code:
module dma_controller(
    input wire [3:0] req,
    input wire [3:0] ack,
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [1:0] active_channel
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        active_channel <= 2'b00; // Reset active channel
    end else begin
        // Grant access to the highest priority request
        case (req)
            4'b0001: active_channel <= 2'b00; // Channel 0
            4'b0010: active_channel <= 2'b01; // Channel 1
            4'b0100: active_channel <= 2'b10; // Channel 2
            4'b1000: active_channel <= 2'b11; // Channel 3
            4'b0011: active_channel <= 2'b00; // Channel 0, priority to 0
            4'b0110: active_channel <= 2'b01; // Channel 1, priority to 1
            4'b1100: active_channel <= 2'b10; // Channel 2, priority to 2
            default: active_channel <= 2'b00; // Default to channel 0
        endcase
    end
end
endmodule

description: Design a Booth multiplier in Verilog that multiplies two 4-bit signed numbers. The output should be an 8-bit signed result. The multiplier should implement the Booth's algorithm to efficiently handle both positive and negative multiplicands.

Design a GPIO controller that can read and write to a 5-bit GPIO port. It should have a mode selection input that decides whether the port is in input mode or output mode. If the mode is set to input mode (mode = 1), the controller should read the value from the GPIO pins and store it in a register. If the mode is set to output mode (mode = 0), the controller should take the value from the register and write it to the GPIO pins. The controller should also have a clock input for synchronization and a reset input to initialize the register to zero.
code:
module gpio_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire mode, // 0 for output mode, 1 for input mode
    input wire [4:0] gpio_input, // GPIO input pins
    output reg [4:0] gpio_output // GPIO output pins
);

    reg [4:0] gpio_reg; // Register to hold GPIO value

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            gpio_reg <= 5'b00000; // Initialize register to zero
            gpio_output <= 5'b00000; // Initialize output to zero
        end else begin
            if (mode) begin
                gpio_reg <= gpio_input; // Read input into register
            end else begin
                gpio_output <= gpio_reg; // Output the value from the register
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit wide multiplexer (MUX) that selects one of four 32-bit input data buses based on a 2-bit select signal. The MUX should output the selected 32-bit data bus.

Design a 32-bit serializer that takes a 32-bit input and serializes it into a single output bit stream. The serializer should serialize one bit per clock cycle. Implement a register that holds the input data and shifts it out one bit at a time on each rising edge of the clock. The output should be valid when the 'valid' signal is high.
code:
module serializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire valid,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    output reg serialized_out
);
    reg [5:0] bit_count; // To track the bit position

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_count <= 0;
            serialized_out <= 0;
        end else if (valid) begin
            serialized_out <= data_in[31 - bit_count]; // Serialize from MSB to LSB
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
            if (bit_count == 31) begin
                bit_count <= 0; // Reset after sending all bits
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a digital phase shifter that takes a 3-bit input and produces a 3-bit output that represents the phase-shifted value. The phase shift should be defined as follows: if the input value is 0, output 1; if the input value is 1, output 2; if the input value is 2, output 3; if the input value is 3, output 4; if the input value is 4, output 5; if the input value is 5, output 6; if the input value is 6, output 7; if the input value is 7, output 0.

Design a simple Turbo encoder that takes a 2-bit input and generates a 4-bit encoded output. The encoder should operate in a way that it applies two independent convolutional encoders in parallel and interleaves their outputs.

Design an I2C controller module in Verilog that handles the start, stop, read, and write signals for communication with an I2C slave device. The controller will have inputs for clock and reset, along with control signals for initiating a read or write operation. It will generate the necessary I2C signals, such as SDA (data line) and SCL (clock line), for up to 8 bits of data transfer and indicate when the transfer is complete.

Design a Verilog module that simulates a thermal sensor calibrator. The circuit should take input in the form of a 10-bit binary value representing the raw temperature reading from the sensor. The output should be a calibrated 10-bit binary value that adjusts the raw reading based on a predefined calibration factor. The calibration factor is defined as an adjustment that is applied to the raw reading. The calibrated output should be the raw reading plus the calibration factor. The calibration factor is also a 10-bit value, and the output should never exceed the maximum value for a 10-bit number (1023). If the output exceeds 1023, it should be capped at 1023.

Design a 16-bit SRAM cell that can read, write, and hold data. The SRAM cell should have inputs for write enable (we), read enable (re), a 16-bit data input (data_in), and a 16-bit address input (addr). It should also have a 16-bit data output (data_out). The SRAM should be able to store data at the specified address when write enable is high, and output the stored data when read enable is high.
code:

description: Design a Watchdog Timer in Verilog. The timer should have an input clock signal and a reset signal. module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire kick,
    output reg timeout
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 4'b0000;
            timeout <= 1'b0;
        end else if (kick) begin
            counter <= 4'b0000; // reset counter on kick
            timeout <= 1'b0; // reset timeout
        end else begin
            if (counter < 4'b1111) begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // increment counter
            end
            
            if (counter == 4'b1111) begin
                timeout <= 1'b1; // set timeout
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module serializer (

    output reg done
);

    reg [7:0] data;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_count <= 3'b000;
            data <= 8'b0;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
            done <= 1'b0;
        end else if (bit_count < 3'd8) begin
            if (bit_count == 3'b000) begin
                data <= parallel_in; // Load data on first clock edge
            end
            serial_out <= data[7 - bit_count]; // Output the bits from MSB to LSB
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count
            done <= (bit_count == 3'd7); // Set done when all bits are sent
        end
    end
endmodule

Implement a restoring divider circuit in Verilog. The divider should take two inputs: a dividend and a divisor, and produce a quotient and a remainder as outputs. The circuit should perform the division using a restoring technique. The divisor should be a positive integer, and the dividend can be any integer value.
code:
module restoring_divider (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input [7:0] dividend,
    input [7:0] divisor,
    output reg [7:0] quotient,
    output reg [7:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);
    reg [7:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg [7:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [7:0] M; // Divisor
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            quotient <= 8'b0;
            remainder <= 8'b0;
            done <= 0;
            A <= 8'b0;
            Q <= 8'b0;
            M <= 8'b0;
            count <= 4'b0;
        end else if (start) begin
            M <= divisor;
            A <= dividend;
            Q <= 8'b0;
            count <= 8; // Assuming 8-bit dividend
            done <= 0;
        end else if (count > 0) begin
            A = {A[6:0], Q[7]}; // Shift A left
            Q = {Q[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift Q left
            A = A - M; // Subtract M from A
            if (A[7] == 1) begin // If A is negative
                A = A + M; // Restore A
                Q[0] = 1'b0; // Set the least significant bit of Q to 0
            end else begin
                Q[0] = 1'b1; // Set the least significant bit of Q to 1
            end
            count = count - 1; // Decrement count
        end else begin
            quotient <= Q; // Final quotient
            remainder <= A; // Final remainder
            done <= 1; // Indicate done
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-input round-robin arbiter. The arbiter should grant access to one of the four requests (req0, req1, req2, req3) in a round-robin fashion. The arbiter should take a clock signal (clk) and a reset signal (rst) as inputs. On each positive edge of the clock, if the reset is not asserted, the arbiter should grant the next available request based on the current grant state. The output should be a 4-bit grant signal (grant), with one bit set to 1 indicating which request is granted.
code:
module round_robin_arbiter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);
    reg [1:0] current_grant;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;
            current_grant <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;  // Reset grant
            // Grant the next available request in round-robin
            case (current_grant)
                2'b00: if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b00; end
                       else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b01; end
                       else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b10; end
                       else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b11; end
                2'b01: if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b01; end
                       else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b10; end
                       else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b11; end
                       else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b00; end
                2'b10: if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b10; end
                       else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b11; end
                       else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b00; end
                       else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b01; end
                2'b11: if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b11; end
                       else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b00; end
                       else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b01; end
                       else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_grant <= 2'b10; end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a simple Kalman filter for sensor fusion. The filter will take two input sensor readings (sensor1 and sensor2), an initial estimate of the state, and an estimate of the error covariance. The output will be the updated estimate of the state and the updated error covariance.

module kalman_filter (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [15:0] sensor1,  
    input [15:0] sensor2,  
    input [15:0] estimate,  
    input [15:0] error_covariance,  
    output reg [15:0] updated_estimate,  
    output reg [15:0] updated_error_covariance  
);  

    reg [15:0] z; // measurement
    reg [15:0] k; // Kalman gain
    reg [15:0] p; // error covariance

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            updated_estimate <= 16'd0;  
            updated_error_covariance <= 16'd0;  
        end else begin  
            z <= (sensor1 + sensor2) >> 1; // simple average of sensors  
            k <= error_covariance / (error_covariance + 16'd1); // assume measurement noise is 1  
            updated_estimate <= estimate + k * (z - estimate);  
            p <= (16'd1 - k) * error_covariance;  
            updated_error_covariance <= p;  
        end  
    end  
endmodule
